forces: A remote peer controls response status, acknowledgment content, timing, and connection failure, so acceptance must be exact, bounded, and fail closed.
The Node binding must prove delivery semantics without acquiring an unapproved socket, HTTP client, host fetch, credential, or third-party runtime dependency.
Attempt identity must preserve canonical event identity without mutating caller-owned event data or implying retry, durability, or exactly-once behavior.
Serialized request bytes and peer-controlled diagnostics must remain bounded and secret-free while result classes stay deterministic for conformance tests.

evidence_ids: in-memory exchange tests observe exactly one call and no live-network dependency
Node scope and dependency checks reject unapproved host and package couplings
all result-class tests assert original event.id and zero-based attempt ordinal without mutating source event
accepted, permanent, retryable, timeout, transport-failure, malformed, ambiguous, and mismatched-acknowledgment fixture arms
oversized projection rejects before exchange and all public failure results exclude peer body and error text

security_justification.audit_integrity: A terminal acknowledgment is recorded only after an exact matching acceptance, preventing a peer response from being mistaken for evidence that this occurrence was handled.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: The handoff does not authenticate or authorize a peer, caller, credential, or request; exchange ownership remains outside the package.
security_justification.authority_provenance: The event identity comes from the canonical occurrence and is preserved unchanged; a peer acknowledgment is accepted only when it binds to that exact identity.
security_justification.concurrency: One handoff invokes its exchange exactly once and creates no queue, retry loop, shared mutable state, or overlapping attempt lifecycle.
security_justification.confidentiality: Request projection is bounded and results expose closed category/code values rather than peer response bodies, headers, URLs, credentials, or error messages.
security_justification.cryptography: No cipher, key, signature, hash, TLS configuration, or credential management is introduced; actual connection security remains caller-owned and out of scope.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Timeout, transport failure, permanent response, and protocol error outcomes use finite codes and do not echo attacker-controlled text.
security_justification.external_security_integration: The injected exchange is a caller-owned port; the package adds no network client, security service, credential store, or external runtime integration.
security_justification.fail_posture: Malformed, ambiguous, missing, duplicate, or mismatched acknowledgment information is terminal protocol error, never acceptance.
security_justification.lifecycle: The module limits itself to one attempt and expressly introduces no retry schedule, queue, backpressure, shutdown drain, socket, or background resource lifecycle.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: The change is bounded to the Node binding, its tests and documentation, and the owning OpenSpec artifacts and capability specification.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: The change serializes an already canonical occurrence for a caller-owned exchange but creates no personal-data collection, transformation policy, or retention store.
security_justification.resource_retention: Request serialization has a fixed bound, failure data is closed, and no connection, timer, buffer, queue, cache, or durable record is retained by the handoff.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: Retryable is only a classified single-attempt result; no retry is scheduled and the unchanged identity is not represented as exactly-once or durable delivery.
security_justification.trust_boundary: The remote peer is attacker-controlled at the exchange boundary, so only exact well-formed acknowledgment of the submitted event ID crosses into accepted state.
